record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: For every isotropic logconcave density f on R^n, is the density at the origin bounded by C^n for some absolute constant C independent of n and f? Equivalently, does there exist an absolute constant C such that f(0) ≤ C^n for every isotropic logconcave density?

evidence.quote: I Conjecture 21 (Slicing). There exists a constant C, such that for an isotropic logconcave density f in R^n, f(0) ≤ C^n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A probability density $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)$ is called logconcave if $\log f$ is concave on its support (with the convention $\log 0=-\infty$). The density $f$ is called isotropic if its associated probability measure has mean zero and identity covariance, i.e.
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x\, f(x)\,dx = 0, \qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x_i x_j\, f(x)\,dx = \delta_{ij} \text{ for all } 1\le i,j\le n.$$
Question (slicing/hyperplane conjecture): Does there exist an absolute constant $C>0$, independent of the dimension $n$ and of the density $f$, such that for every $n\ge 1$ and every isotropic logconcave density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$f(0) \le C^n\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Bourgain's slicing (hyperplane) conjecture, equivalent to the existence of a universal constant C with f(0) ≤ C^n for every isotropic logconcave density on R^n, was affirmatively resolved in late 2024. Klartag and Lehec, building on a stochastic-localization small-ball bound of Qingyang Guan and stability estimates of Eldan–Mikulincer, established the conjecture; an alternative proof via small-ball estimates was given by Bizeul (arXiv:2501.06854, 2025).

status_evidence.title: Qingyang Guan, Joseph Lehec and Bo'az Klartag Solved The Slice Conjecture!
status_evidence.snippet: Guan, Lehec and Klartag solved Bourgain's slicing conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The slicing conjecture has been solved (2024).

status_evidence.title: Affirmative Resolution of Bourgain's Slicing Problem using Guan's Bound
status_evidence.snippet: Final step in the resolution of Bourgain's slicing problem in the affirmative, using Guan's bound and stability estimates.
status_evidence.claim: Klartag–Lehec affirmatively resolved the slicing problem.

status_evidence.title: The slicing conjecture via small ball estimates
status_evidence.snippet: Alternative proof of the slicing conjecture via small ball probability estimates for isotropic log-concave measures.
status_evidence.claim: An alternative proof of the slicing conjecture was given in 2025.
